parsed.attack: The invitation goes to siblings two and three, and what they receive - 'Sarah rang Tuesday, you are up next' - is the entire product delivered inside the body of a text message; installing adds nothing except that the ledger now points at them. The person whose behaviour the ledger exists to change is the sibling doing less, and you are asking that exact person to opt into a permanent, timestamped, family-visible record of their own under-contribution: a negative-value install, answered with 'ok, will call Sunday'. Even at perfect conversion the graph closes at three, no sibling ever invites a non-sibling, so the household-to-household coefficient is exactly zero and every new family is one the founder recruits by hand.
parsed.strongest_defence: The second sibling installs for the opposite reason - the initiator is almost always the resentful over-contributor, and being able to make one's own calls visible is what the under-credited sibling wants; a family ask carries weight no marketing message does and closes within days.
parsed.verdict_reason: The in-family invite can convert, but the graph terminates at three people and produces no mechanism at all for reaching the next household.
